beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — the fluent-wrong note shown as if approved
beats.narration_text: Revenue is down this quarter because enterprise renewals slipped. That sentence has no source behind it, and it was about to go in a board deck.

props.command: claude "draft a variance note explaining the Q3 revenue miss for the board deck"
output: "Revenue is down 8% QoQ, driven by enterprise renewal timing."
No source file cited. No owner named. No period boundary stated.

beats.role_note: stakes before any fix is shown
beats.narration_text: Method: a variance note becomes evidence only when it ties to a source, a period, and an owner who can be asked how they know. Use this test before anything goes in a deck. Where it fails: a fluent sentence and a sourced sentence look identical on the page. The confidence of the language tells you nothing about whether the underlying number was ever checked.
beats.visual_intent: A single sentence card, then a red X appears over it labeled 'no source', 'no period', 'no owner' one at a time

beats.narration_text: The fix is structural, not a reminder to be careful. A phase gate splits preparation from judgment: the machine drafts, computes, and flags. A named human reads the flagged items, ties them to a source, and decides if the note is ready. The gate is not a formality — it is the point where accountability actually enters the artifact.

Verified means four things exist together: a named source file, the period it covers, a control total that ties to the general ledger, and an owner who will stand behind the number. Missing any one of these, the sentence is an assertion, not evidence — no matter how confident it sounds.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — a runnable prompt, read and discussed
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take a variance note you've actually seen go into a deck, and paste it in with this prompt: pull out every factual claim, and for each one, name the source, period, and owner it would need to count as verified — or mark it unsupported. Read what comes back before you trust any of it.

props.command: claude "For this variance note, list every factual claim. For each, name the source file, period, and owner it would need to be verified — or mark it unsupported: [PASTE YOUR NOTE]"
